past_actions.summary: Enroll in an online continuing education module on commercial and small business lending — a skill adjacent to my current auto loan focus but one that would broaden my portfolio relevance inside the bank. Two hours per week, self-paced. No cost through the bank's professional development benefit.

Send a carefully worded memo to Regional VP Sandra Okafor flagging the RoboRide Phase 2 rumor as an unconfirmed market signal with potential implications for the branch's auto loan portfolio. Frame it as a proactive risk flag, not a crisis. Request a 30-minute call to discuss whether other branches in the region are seeing similar signals. Attach a brief one-page scenario sketch showing what a 15% and 30% decline in auto loan origination volume would mean for branch P&L over 12 months.
past_actions.emotional_state: focused, controlled urgency — not alarmed but no longer passively monitoring

past_actions.summary: Send a follow-up communication to Sandra Okafor — not another memo, but a direct request for a 20-minute call this week. Reference the Maria Santos public statement and the RoboRide Phase 2 confirmation as the reason for urgency. Attach an updated scenario model with a third scenario added: 50% decline in auto loan origination over 18 months, reflecting a more aggressive adoption curve. Make clear I am ready to present a branch-level response plan if she wants one. Frame it as seeking alignment, not asking permission.
past_actions.emotional_state: deliberate urgency — the situation has clarified and I am moving with precision, not speed for its own sake. Privately more unsettled than I show at work.

past_actions.summary: Formalize the written auto loan underwriting criteria document that Patricia Hawkins requested following my tick 3 proactive disclosure call. Produce a one-page written summary of the revised underwriting parameters: minimum credit score threshold (raised by 10 points), maximum loan term for vehicles over 3 years old (60 months, reduced from 72), and the enhanced review requirement for floor plan facilities. The document is factual, professional, and framed as standard portfolio management policy — not a punitive measure directed at any specific account. Send it to Patricia with a brief cover note acknowledging that clarity serves both parties. This is relationship banking: she asked for the parameters in writing, I provide them promptly.

Draft and submit to Sandra Okafor the branch-level portfolio stress response plan I offered in tick 2. The document covers three components: (1) a delinquency triage protocol for existing auto loan accounts — tiered by employment sector exposure, flagging accounts in auto manufacturing, dealership, and auto-adjacent services for enhanced monitoring and proactive outreach before they miss a payment; (2) a non-auto lending activation roadmap for the branch, targeting SBA-adjacent small business loans, home equity products, and personal lending — product lines I now have coursework grounding in after five months of the commercial lending module; (3) a 12-month volume replacement projection showing how the branch can offset 30% of auto loan origination decline through product diversification. Frame it as a branch evolution plan, not a crisis document. Send it with a direct note: I am ready to present this in person or on a call, and I am requesting authority to begin activating the non-auto product lines within my existing underwriting mandate.

Reach out directly to Kevin O'Brien to receive and review the one-page brief he has prepared. Frame it as a collegial professional conversation — not as a manager checking in, but as a peer who respects the work he has done. I want to understand what he has written and whether it relates to my position change, the branch situation, or something else. This is also an opportunity to be honest with him: I am no longer in the branch manager seat and he should know that before he hears it through other channels. Maintaining his trust is more valuable now than managing appearances.

Follow up directly with Linda Park on the tick 7 outreach — not a second ask, but a brief, professional note acknowledging the RoboRide expansion as the context for my outreach. Frame it: I reached out last week because I saw this coming, and this week confirms the trajectory. The point is not to say 'I told you so' — it is to demonstrate that I understand the market with precision, that I can be useful to anyone in the regional financial services space who needs someone who can read disruption early. Ask specifically whether she has heard of any credit union, community bank, or insurance-adjacent finance roles in the region — and offer to share the scenario models I built at First Community as context for any conversation she facilitates. This is active relationship management, not passive networking.

Complete the final SBA 7(a) modules in the commercial lending coursework — credential milestone push after 9 months of study. Simultaneously send Kevin O'Brien a peer message offering to walk him through SBA product underwriting basics as he pursues his portfolio expansion. Draft and send first cold outreach to Millfield Community Credit Union small business lending team — targeted, no posted job, specific pitch around disruption-driven demand for community credit. Deferred Linda Park follow-up to tick 10 when I will have the credential in hand.
past_actions.emotional_state: focused, quietly urgent — the runway is real but still long enough to be deliberate

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in and I am unemployed. I spent the first five months doing everything a careful, proactive manager is supposed to do — flagged the risk early, ran the scenario models, built the relationships, studied the adjacent skills, wrote the plan. None of it prevented the outcome. The auto lending market is contracting and the bank made a structural decision, whether or not my plan influenced it. What I have learned: being right about the risk does not protect your position. Acting on the right information still exposes you to institutional forces you cannot fully see. The 2008 lesson — trust is fragile — applies here. I trusted that competence and proactivity would be rewarded with stability. That was a mistake in the environment of a shrinking revenue line.
reflections.identity_shift: I came into this as a branch manager — that identity was load-bearing for me (0.6 identity attachment). That role is gone now. I am not yet sure what replaces it. 'Finance professional in transition' is accurate but feels like a placeholder. The coursework has given me something: I am becoming someone with broader lending skills, not just an auto loan specialist. That may be the seed of a new identity if I let it grow. I am less attached to the title than I thought I would be — the loss stings, but I am not collapsing.
regrets: I did not build a stronger external network earlier — my connections are almost all tied to the auto ecosystem, which is exactly the sector under stress. I should have been cultivating relationships at community banks and credit unions before I needed them.

I may have pushed too hard with Sandra Okafor too visibly. The memos and scenario models were correct, but I may have signaled that I saw the branch's core product as a failing enterprise — which made me expendable rather than valuable.

I did not have a cleaner read on my own job security. The role_security score was 0.36 — I knew it was low. I should have accelerated the job search earlier rather than investing entirely in saving the branch.
successes: Started the commercial lending coursework at tick 0 — already 30% complete. That decision looks better every month.
Maintained honest communication with Kevin O'Brien, my highest-trust contact. That relationship is intact and may be the most useful thing I have right now.

Ran scenario models before the crisis deepened — even if they did not save my job, they sharpened my own thinking and I can walk into any interview and explain what happened to auto lending in Millfield with precision.
Did not panic. Six ticks of controlled, proportional responses. That discipline is real and I can carry it forward.
reflections.adaptation_notes: I am adapting, not freezing. The evidence: I enrolled in coursework before the disruption was certain, I escalated through proper channels, I am now moving toward job search rather than waiting for the phone to ring. But I am also not fully a hustler — I am working the network carefully rather than throwing applications everywhere. This fits who I am. The risk is that careful adaptation is too slow if the runway shrinks faster than I expect. I need to watch the burn rate and not let the 24-month cushion make me complacent.

reflections.reflection: Nine months in. Four unemployed. Savings have dropped roughly $28,000 since I lost the job — from about $182,000 to $154,000. The burn is steady and real. I have been deliberate, not panicked, and I believe that is still correct. But this tick forced me to look at something uncomfortable: the branch is moving on without me. Kevin O'Brien — my most trusted colleague — is formally requesting a portfolio expansion into exactly the product lines I spent five months studying and proposing. He is doing it through whoever is the interim manager now. He did not call me first. That is not a betrayal — it is how institutions work. He has his own career to manage. But it means I am no longer a resource to the branch even informally. I am fully outside now.
reflections.identity_shift: The coursework credential is the pivot. I have been in a liminal state — not a branch manager anymore, not yet anything with a clear name. The SBA 7(a) certificate, once I complete it this month, gives me something to stand behind that is forward-looking rather than backward-referencing. I am not 'former branch manager.' I am 'commercial lending professional with SBA origination credentials.' That is a different sentence. I am beginning to feel more like the latter than the former, which is progress. The identity attachment score of 0.6 to the branch manager role — that number is lower now, maybe 0.35. The role is gone and I am not grieving it the way I expected to. I am more focused on what comes next.
regrets: I have now spent nine months in the community and my only real external relationship is Linda Park, who is managing her own disruption and not in a position to help me. I should have started building credit union and community bank relationships at tick 6 or 7, not tick 9. Every month of delay on that front is a month of compounding absence from those networks.

I deferred the cold outreach to community lending institutions too long. I was waiting until I felt 'ready' — until the credential was complete, until Linda had given me a signal, until the right moment. There is no right moment. The right moment was months ago.
successes: The coursework discipline has held for nine consecutive months. 50% progress, almost complete. This was not guaranteed — unemployed people often let self-directed study slip. I did not.

Kevin O'Brien relationship remains warm. His portfolio expansion move is actually a validation of the SBA product analysis I shared with him. He absorbed the information and is acting on it. That is a kind of influence even without a title.

I did not mass-apply to every bank in a fifty-mile radius in a panic. The targeted approach is still correct. I have one institution to contact this month — the credit union — and I am going in with a specific, credentialed pitch, not a desperate one.
Recognized that Linda Park is not a lead-generator right now and adjusted accordingly rather than continuing to press her. Reading social signals accurately is a skill.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The adaptation pattern is consistent: deliberate, credential-focused, relationship-preserving, not panicked. The gap in this pattern is the external institution outreach — I have been too inward-focused. The credit union cold contact this tick is the first real step outside the old professional network. If I get no response in two ticks I need to expand to two or three institutions simultaneously. I cannot afford to treat each contact as a one-at-a-time sequential process if the runway starts feeling shorter. Current runway: 22 months. At my burn rate I have enough time to be deliberate, but not enough time to be passive. The distinction matters.
